finding.claim: SQL injection via unsanitized ORDER BY clause in list_users_sorted. The sort parameter is concatenated directly into the query, allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. subquery-based boolean/blind extraction from other tables, or error-based leakage).
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) at list.php:6

trace.note: $sort concatenated into SQL string and executed via PDO::query

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, casting, quoting, or escaping on the path. Prepared statements are not used here (ORDER BY cannot be bound as a parameter anyway). Contrast list_users_safe (line 10-11) which uses an allowlist map, and find_user (line 16-17) which uses a bound parameter; both are safe. No authentication/authorization check exists in the file either.

verdict.reason: list.php:5-6 takes $_GET['sort'] and concatenates it into the ORDER BY query with no allowlist or escaping; the allowlist at list.php:10-11 is in the separate list_users_safe function, and no authentication exists. The function has no callers in this directory, so reachability depends on code outside it, but any caller would pass the raw parameter.
